To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of glucan and local anaesthetics is advantageous for impregnation of wound dressings.

the combination of trimetoprime with sulfadimidine and local anaesthetics is suitable for the preparation of wound dressings, and that the release of chlorohexidin is more advantageous from Natrosol dispersions.
the use of a combination of local anaesthetics with trimetoprim-sulfadimidine is more effective than the use of local anaestetics alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new type of impregnated wound dressing.
the development of a new type of impregnated wound covers, the preparation and properties of which are discussed.
the development of a wound dressing impregnated with an antimicrobial agent, a local anaesthetic and glucan.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of antimicrobial agents with local anaesthetics and immunomodulating substances, in the presence of a hydrophilic carrier, is a suitable method for the preparation of impregnated wound covers.
the dispersions of Natrosol are more suitable as carriers for impregnation of textiles for wound dressing.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of antimicrobial drugs with local anaesthetics and immunomodulating substances is advantageous, as is also the use of macromolecular hydrophilic gels for the impregnated wound dressing.
a combination of antimicrobially effective substances, local anaesthetics and fungal glucan is suitable for the impregnations of textile carriers.
the dispersions of hydrophilic macromo- lecular substances are suitable for the impregnating of wound coverings with antimicro- bial and local anaesthetics substances.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of a polymer for impregnation depends on the type of drug and its liberation kinetics.
the use of glucan in the form of a dispersion is a promising way of increasing the antimicrobial efficacy and accelerating the liberation of active substances.
the choice of the polymer for the impregnated dressing should take account of the physicochemical characteristics of both the drug and the carrier.
